diagnosis.conclusion: The evaluator incorrectly rejected a genuinely completed admitted command solely because native post observation arrived later. That coverage stop precedes and explains the subsequent recorded ledger-stopped pre-hook errors.
causalLimits: This proves the evaluator ordering defect, not the entire 122.077699-second timeout cause.
Two delayed post settlements do not prove full native or physical process closure.
The retained public execution is not an original sample or a quality comparison.

sourceAssessment: Admission stores the native turn digest alongside existing tool/name/thread identity. A new terminal-before-post settlement requires commandExecution, an admitted canonical exec, the same nonempty native thread and turn, completed status and a safe-integer exit code. Unknown, cancelled, mismatched or nonterminal command notifications fail closed.
Dispatch and settlement remain separate from task success: a nonzero command exit code is retained and still proves attempted execution. A pre-permit or item/started alone does not mark dispatch.
Matching duplicate command terminals retain the first settlement time; changed terminal metadata stops coverage. A mismatched command completion after settlement also stops coverage.

Post observations reject cancelled rows and name/thread/turn mismatches before any promotion. The loader uses the existing native normalizeNativeHookToolName for post names. A matching late post preserves terminal metadata and the original settlement time.

Existing native policy, authority, trusted relay construction, admission/retention stop checks, model/calendar binding and original cap remain. Native physical authority and cleanup uncertain are not overridden.
